# task-e2484ef1: shift grid down one row

## Confirmed rule
Translate the entire input grid downward by exactly one row. Keep every cell in its original column and preserve its color. Fill the top row with the background color, and clip the original bottom row. Keep the grid dimensions unchanged.

## Demonstration
Input (3×3):
```
5 5 5
5 5 0
5 5 5
```
Output:
```
5 5 5
5 5 5
5 5 0
```
The lone 0 moves down one row; other cells remain background 5.

## Additional confirmed demonstration
A 23×2 demo used background 9 and sparse 0 cells. In 1-indexed coordinates, the input had zeros at (row 10, col 1), (11, 1), (12, 2), and (13, 2); the output had them at (11, 1), (12, 1), (13, 2), and (14, 2), with all other cells unchanged. This independently confirms a one-row downward translation of all cells, not an object-specific move or recoloring.

## Application and validation
For each future instance of this task, identify its background color from the grid, set output row 0 to that color, and copy input rows 0 through H−2 into output rows 1 through H−1. Discard any non-background content in the final input row rather than wrapping it. Preserve width and height; verify every output row has the same width as the input and compare each output row against the source row immediately above it.

Confirmed on a 4×11 test and the 23×2 demonstration above; a 15×30 instance and a 22×25 instance with background 2 were also accepted with the exact downward shift. A 19×19 instance with background 5 and a dense, irregular color-6 shape was also accepted using the same rule. A further 16×23 instance (background 8, foreground 6, dense irregular pattern) was accepted with exact shift: output row 0 all 8; output rows 1–15 exact copies of input rows 0–14; final source row discarded. This is a one-row translation, not a recoloring or object-specific operation. An additional 20×6 test with background 2 and a dense irregular color-6 region was accepted with zero wrong attempts: output row 0 was all 2; output rows 1–19 exactly copied input rows 0–18; input row 19 was clipped. The dense foreground region does not change the rule.

## Transcription caution
The first submission on this 16×23 instance was incorrect, despite applying the right transformation, because input row 0 was mistyped: it has 6 at columns 8 and 10–18 (1-indexed), with 8 at column 9 and columns 19–23. A corrected exact transcription plus the shift was accepted. For densely printed grids, verify source rows carefully and enforce each row's stated width before generating the shifted output.

## Submission validation pitfall
